text:
olivia: heads up — noticed a weird edge case in the console when combining per-route quotas with scoped roles. users with a scoped 'read:routes' role can see quota widgets but can't edit the routing policy, which makes the dashboard show 0/0 and confuses support. :confused:
marco: ugh. is that a UI-only visibility bug or an authz check in the quota API?
olivia: looks like both. console calls /api/routes/:id/quota (returns 403) but the frontend still renders the quota card because feature flag says 'show_quota_card'.
anya: product question — do we want the quota card to be hidden entirely if the user lacks modify permission? or show read-only metrics and a tooltip saying "request access"?
sam: my 2c: for enterprise tenants we should show read-only metrics where possible. Hiding feels like data loss. But if the API returns 403, frontend has to handle it gracefully (don't treat as missing data).
marco: agree. if API returns 403 we should map it to a 200+empty payload or a specific error object so UI can differentiate: {"quota":null, "permission":"readonly"} vs real 404.
olivia: yep — currently backend returns 403 with no body. can we add a small contract change to respond with 200 + "access_level" header or a tiny body? that avoids a full-blown API version bump.
marco: we can. propose: when user has read but not write, return 200 with {"quota": {...}, "access_level":"read"}. when no access return 404. when resource exists but user truly forbidden (e.g., tenant block) return 403.
anya: that seems reasonable. add a console UX note: show metrics, disable edit controls, and add an CTA "Request edit access" that opens a modal for tenant admins. :+1:
sam: telemetry note — we need an event for "quota_card_rendered" with access_level so we can measure how many users see read-only vs editable. that will inform rollout.
marco: good call. also we should sample traces so we can link a render event to the backend authorization rule applied. maybe add a log field authz_rule="scope:routes.modify".
olivia: could be useful for debugging. small concern: we already emit a lot of authz logs; prefer sampling 1% by default and allow 100% sampling per-tenant via feature flag for enterprise debugging.
marco: agreed. I'll add sampling config in authn service — default 0.01. and expose a temporary canary route param ?authz_debug=1 for internal sessions.
anya: rollout plan: change backend to return access_level read/write, console patch to honor it, and enable telemetry. we feature-flag the console behavior and do a staged rollout to 10% of orgs for 48h, then check metrics.
sam: what metrics: errors (render failures), support tickets (via tagging), traffic to quota endpoints, and the telemetry event counts. also break down by role type (service-account vs user).
marco: implementation question — does our RBAC middleware know about "read vs write" at the granularity we need? current scopes are bit-flags: routes.read, routes.modify. middleware returns allowed_scopes list. backend can map that to access_level easily.
olivia: does this require any tenant migration? i.e., existing policies that use route-level overrides?
marco: no migration; just derive from the existing scope check. however edge case: delegated admins with temporary sudo — they currently get a proxy token; middleware sees full scopes but console runs as the user and expects limited view. we should ensure the access_level reflects the effective principal used by the UI call.
sam: note for docs: update "Console RBAC" doc to include access_level semantics and UX examples (screenshots). also add a snippet for customer support to explain why a card might be view-only.
olivia: I'll draft the PRs: 1) authn service contract change + tests, 2) console change behind flag + basic e2e, 3) telemetry event + sampling config.
anya: timeline?
marco: I can start the backend change today, should be a small patch — expect code + tests by EOD tomorrow.
sam: I'll do the console PR on Thursday; want to pair with olivia for the modal CTA flow.
olivia: cool. can we add a tiny integration test that simulates a 403 -> 200(access_level=read) so we don't regress?
marco: yes. add unit test in authz and an integration in api-gateway that asserts header/body mapping.
anya: last ask — for the rollout gating, add a telemetry alert if "quota_card_rendered:read" / "quota_card_rendered:write" ratio shifts > 10% unexpectedly. catches policy misconfig.
sam: noted. will add an alert dashboard panel in Console Operations.
marco: I'll drop a quick PR link when ready. olivia, can you add the initial checklist to the rollout doc and ping #release-war-room when we flip the flag?
olivia: will do. thanks all :rocket:
sre-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary flag flip for feature/console-quota-access-level at 2025-11-02T09:00Z (can be canceled within 15m).
